active_dispute_risk_definition.definition: A dispute is ACTIVE if dispute_status is one of active_statuses AND closed_at_utc IS NULL. active_dispute_risk for a scoped object is TRUE if ANY ACTIVE dispute exists for that scope.

Explicit admin override MAY bypass active_dispute_risk only via a recorded DisputeRiskOverride with sealed evidence and explicit approver identity. Overrides MUST be scoped, time-bounded, and auditable.

If a provider dispute/chargeback targets a checkout_group payment spanning multiple Orders, the platform MUST allocate dispute_amount_minor and provider fees across Orders using AllocationRule=PROPORTIONAL_ORDER_GROSS_V1 with immutable ProviderAllocation entries; MUST NOT apply FX.

dispute_risk_fail_closed.must: Active dispute risk MUST be treated as a fail-closed risk flag for all automated authorities; only explicit admin override records may bypass within bounded scope and time.

Dispute risk MUST NOT be inferred from free-form text; it MUST be derived from DisputeStatus + closed_at_utc per definition.

money.allocation_rule_required: When a provider event impacts multiple Orders, PAY-3 MUST allocate minor-unit amounts deterministically per Order using AllocationRule=PROPORTIONAL_ORDER_GROSS_V1 and persist immutable ProviderAllocation records.
money.chargeback_platform_loss_default: Chargebacks are treated as platform loss by default (unless a separate, explicitly-locked organizer chargeback penalty is configured).
money.checkout_group_single_currency: A single provider payment attempt/capture/refund/dispute MUST NOT span Orders of different currencies. If encountered, system MUST fail-closed with ERR_VALIDATION / ORD_CHECKOUT_GROUP_CURRENCY_MISMATCH. FX is out of scope.
money.fee_allocation_rounding: Allocation rounding MUST be deterministic (largest remainder; stable tie-break by price_line_id ascending).
money.fee_allocation_two_tier: Fee allocation MUST be line-level for refunds/disputes, and order-level for settlement/payout; sums MUST reconcile deterministically.
money.gateway_fees_platform_borne: Payment provider (gateway) fees are platform-borne and MUST NOT reduce org payout except via explicit chargeback/penalty policy.
money.platform_fee_basis_ticket_excl_tax: Percent platform fees MUST be computed on ticket_price_excl_tax (not on ticket VAT).
money.platform_fee_non_refundable_default: Platform fees are non-refundable by default; refunding fees requires explicit override reason + ledger postings.
money.platform_fee_supply_to_payer: Platform fee supply counterparty MUST equal payer_mode (supply to payer).

concurrency_control.assertion: UPDATE fieldN SET total_refunded = total_refunded + amount WHERE total_refunded + amount <= total_captured AND currency matches.

rules: Refund amount + currency must be validated against server-side truth (captured/settled totals).
Refunds must be safe under concurrency; use locking/optimistic concurrency per LOCKS-1 when updating totals.
Refund creation must emit EVT-1 events after commit.

If a provider refund is issued against a checkout_group payment that covers multiple Orders, the platform MUST allocate refund_amount_minor to affected Orders using AllocationRule=PROPORTIONAL_ORDER_GROSS_V1 and record ProviderAllocation entries before posting to LED-1/REFUND-1 intents.

GC-001: late-capture reversal MUST use Refund.reason_code in {LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_HOLD_EXPIRED, LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_GRACE_EXPIRED}; fee posture: platform_fee MUST be refunded; provider fees MUST be refunded/voided when provider capabilities allow; reversal MUST be idempotent per refund idempotency rules.

rules.text: Platform-issued identifiers MUST be UUIDv7-based. PAY-3-issued IDs MUST use an explicit prefix registry: refund_id=ref_<uuid_v7>, dispute_id=dsp_<uuid_v7>, evidence_pack_id=epk_<uuid_v7>, provider_event_receipt_id=per_<uuid_v7>. IDs that reference other domain contracts (order_id, payment_intent_id) MUST be bare UUIDv7 (see ORD-1 / PAY-2). Provider-originated identifiers (provider_event_id, provider_refund_id, provider_case_id) MUST NOT be constrained to UUID formats.
Ledger hooks: ticketing.ledger.post_refund.v1, ticketing.ledger.post_dispute_open.v1

rules.rationale: Avoid expanding PCI scope and catastrophic data exposure.
rules.text: No PAN/CVV/sensitive authentication data may be stored. Token-only, hosted payment methods preferred.

rules.rationale: Prevents cross-tenant money movement and enumeration.
rules.text: All refund/dispute actions and reads MUST be tenant-scoped. Missing tenant context => ERR_FORBIDDEN; cross-tenant reads => ERR_NOT_FOUND (hide existence).

rules.rationale: Retries and duplicated webhooks are normal; dedupe must be durable.
rules.text: Refund actions, dispute ingestion, and evidence submission MUST be idempotent and parameter-consistent. Provider events MUST be durably deduped by provider_event_id.

rules.rationale: Prevents irreversible financial loss from concurrent partial refunds.
rules.text: Refund totals MUST never exceed captured/settled totals and MUST match the original currency. Sum-of-parts validation MUST use atomic arithmetic predicates (no read-then-write).

rules.rationale: Evidence integrity is required for disputes and audits.
rules.text: Evidence packs MUST be immutable after sealing. Artifact set is append-only pre-seal; seal produces a hash manifest and disallows mutation.

rules.rationale: Provider is source of truth; local contradictions cause wrong financial postings.
rules.text: Dispute state transitions MUST be provider-truth authoritative; out-of-order provider events MUST NOT regress terminal states.

rules.rationale: Providers can include the same settlement item in multiple reports (pending/finalized); global dedupe prevents double-counting and double-posting.
rules.text: Settlement lines MUST be globally unique by (provider, provider_settlement_id). Duplicates across reports/batches MUST NOT trigger LED-1 posting and MUST be recorded as ignored duplicates (or rejected).

rules.rationale: Prevents denial-of-service from heavy CPU/IO in request path.
rules.text: Evidence hashing/manifest generation MUST be performed asynchronously via OBQC-1. HTTP request handlers MUST NOT synchronously hash evidence artifacts.

Single-currency checkout groups: a single provider payment attempt/capture/refund/dispute MUST NOT be applied across Orders with different currency. If detected, MUST fail-closed with ERR_VALIDATION / ORD_CHECKOUT_GROUP_CURRENCY_MISMATCH; MUST NOT attempt FX.

Deterministic allocation: if a provider-level amount (fee/refund/dispute) references multiple Orders, the platform MUST allocate minor-unit amounts using AllocationRule=PROPORTIONAL_ORDER_GROSS_V1 and persist immutable ProviderAllocation rows. Allocation MUST be reproducible; rounding remainder MUST be assigned deterministically (stable sort by order_id, remainder to first).

Ledger fan-out: PAY-driven ledger postings MUST be posted per Order/org (never as a single checkout_group posting). PAY-3 MUST invoke LED-1 posting intents/templates per Order allocation to preserve COA boundaries and multi-tenancy.

GC-001 late capture remediation: if a provider confirms capture/settlement for a payment_attempt after the associated SeatHold has expired (or after any bounded payment-grace window), the system MUST NOT issue admission rights or allocate inventory. It MUST enqueue an automatic reversal (void if possible; otherwise refund) using RefundReasonCode LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_HOLD_EXPIRED or LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_GRACE_EXPIRED, and MUST emit ERR_VALIDATION / PAY_LATE_CAPTURE_AFTER_HOLD_EXPIRED (ERR-1) for correlation.

rules.rationale: System must degrade safely without losing events or leaking money.
rules.text: Refund/dispute storms and webhook burst traffic MUST degrade safely using OBS-1 observed flags. When OBS-1 observed flag PAYOUT_FREEZE=true, payout/settlement release operations in the payments domain MUST be blocked with ERR_UNAVAILABLE and subcode OBS_DEGRADED_MODE_BLOCKED (ERR-1), while webhook ingestion and ProviderEventReceipt persistence MUST remain enabled. When OBS-1 observed flag HOT_SALE_MODE=true, webhook ingestion MAY apply backpressure/rate limits, but MUST NOT drop events; events MUST either be accepted and queued or rejected deterministically with ERR_UNAVAILABLE (OBS_DEGRADED_MODE_BLOCKED) and MUST be retryable. Queue backlog, receipt processing lag, and dedupe rejection rate MUST be emitted as telemetry and MUST alert within 24 hours; if sustained beyond 72 hours, the incident MUST be escalated per GOV-0.

rules.rationale: Makes money flows debuggable without increasing risk.
rules.text: Refund/dispute/reconciliation actions MUST emit Ash.Tracer spans and bounded metrics; labels MUST NOT include PII or secrets.

rules.rationale: Prevents silent margin/liquidity loss and operational overwhelm.
rules.text: System MUST detect refund-rate spikes, dispute-open spikes, and reconciliation value-at-risk; alerts MUST be SEV2.

rules.rationale: Preserves forensic evidence for phantom/misrouted webhooks.
rules.text: Verified but unbound provider events MUST NOT be silently deleted on TTL expiry; they MUST be moved to a permanent audit sink and emit an investigation signal.
Provider enum values MUST match provider_registry.provider_id exactly
Canonical resources: DisputeEvidencePack, ProviderRefundEvent, ProviderDisputeEvent
Cross-tenant reads return ERR_NOT_FOUND per TEN-1
All *_at_utc fields MUST be utc_datetime_usec (RFC3339 UTC microseconds Z)
ProviderEventReceipt uniqueness: (org_id, provider, provider_event_id)
Webhook signature comparison MUST use constant-time compare on canonical body bytes

rules.rationale: Prevents fraud/chargeback arbitrage and ensures consistent enterprise-safe posture across offline/online flows.
rules.text: If any ACTIVE dispute exists for an order/payment attempt, systems SHALL treat it as a risk flag and MUST fail-closed for refunds, transfers, reissues, and payout execution unless a valid explicit admin DisputeRiskOverride exists for that specific scope.

rules.rationale: Maintains auditability and prevents automation from weakening risk posture.
rules.text: Dispute risk overrides MUST be explicit admin actions with sealed evidence, approver identity, and expiry; automated authorities MUST NOT create overrides.
Fee evaluation MUST resolve an applicable FeeScheduleRevision (org default, with optional event override) or raise PAY_FEE_SCHEDULE_NOT_FOUND.
Percent fees MUST use ticket_price_excl_tax basis; implementations MUST NOT compute fees on the VAT portion of ticket price.
Fee payer_mode MUST be one of {buyer, org}. Supply counterparty MUST equal payer_mode.
Provider fee allocation MUST record basis_amount_minor and support deterministic line-level allocations for refunds/disputes.
Allocation sums MUST reconcile exactly after deterministic rounding; otherwise raise PAY_FEE_ALLOCATION_SUM_MISMATCH.

Fee/Ledger atomicity: When PAY-3 transitions a payment/fee outcome that results in ledger writes, the Redis hot-path state (e.g., payment intent dedupe keys, provider-event receipt caches, temporary auth locks) MUST NOT be cleared unless and until the corresponding Postgres write-through truth (LED-1 hook/outbox record) is durable. If true cross-store atomic commit is unavailable, PAY-3 MUST implement a crash-safe handover using a Postgres outbox as the source of truth and a Redis tombstone pattern (idempotent) to prevent double-entry on retry and to prevent phantom 'in-flight' states after crash.

in_scope: Dispute/chargeback ingestion and lifecycle state tracking
Evidence pack creation/sealing and immutable audit
Provider webhook signature verification + replay safety

summary: Defines tenant-safe refunds and dispute lifecycles, verified webhook ingestion, immutable evidence handling with async sealing, and a multi-provider reconciliation loop that prevents settlement replay double-counting and blocks ledger double-posting, with Ash 3.x concurrency rules and CI-enforced denial tests.
